summary:
Orbit Health is an offline-capable health dashboard designed to help astronauts monitor and manage their health during long-duration space missions. It allows astronauts to record daily measurements, identify unusual readings, review health trends, and conduct targeted follow-ups. The dashboard tracks seven health indicators, including oxygen saturation and daily radiation exposure, while providing space-specific measurement guidance and recommended actions based on mission protocols.

When an indicator falls outside its demonstration range, Orbit Health highlights the affected trend points and provides structured Recheck, Take Action, and Seek Help guidance. Follow-up records remain linked to the original measurement without duplicating values that were not remeasured. All data is stored locally and can be exported as JSON or CSV.

By supporting early detection of potential health risks and informed self-assessment, Orbit Health empowers astronauts to take a more active role in managing their health, particularly during missions where communication with Earth may be delayed or limited.
details:
Orbit Health is an offline-capable health monitoring application designed to help astronauts independently assess their health and maintain accurate health records during long-duration space missions, particularly when communication with Earth is delayed or limited.

The application enables astronauts to record seven health and environmental indicators: resting heart rate, systolic blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, oxygen saturation, and daily radiation exposure. Each indicator includes an expandable measurement guide with the required equipment, step-by-step instructions, and space-specific tips to guide astronauts in taking measurements during space missions.

After each check-in, Orbit Health compares the recorded measurements against demonstration ranges and highlights indicators requiring attention. Unhealthy readings are identified through both text and colour coding. Interactive trend charts allow astronauts to visualise changes over time, with unhealthy data points and their adjacent line segments highlighted in red, while healthy portions remain green. The "Actions to Take" section provides indicator-specific guidance organised into Recheck, Take Action, Seek Help, and Space Tip categories. Additionally, a symptoms checkbox prioritises reported symptoms over measurement-range feedback, helping astronauts recognise potential health concerns even when their readings fall within the expected ranges.

Orbit Health also features a targeted follow-up system that allows astronauts to reassess specific unhealthy indicators without repeating the entire health check-in. Previously recorded measurements for other indicators remain accessible with their original timestamps but are not duplicated into new records. This helps prevent older measurements from being mistaken for current readings and preserves the accuracy of measurement timestamps. Other unresolved unhealthy indicators continue displaying their respective follow-up recommendations.

To support missions with limited connectivity, Orbit Health stores records locally in the browser and allows users to export their health data in JSON or CSV formats. Versioned JSON exports preserve record IDs, follow-up relationships, timestamps, notes, and measurements, supporting health record continuity. The application also uses a service worker to cache its interface, enabling offline access after the application has been successfully loaded and cached.

Orbit Health was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript modules, SVG charts, browser localStorage, a service worker, and a small Node.js development server. It operates without third-party runtime dependencies or a backend service, making it a lightweight application suitable for offline use.

By integrating health monitoring, visual trend analysis, and space-specific guidance into a single platform, Orbit Health aims to make health assessments more accessible and manageable for astronauts. Its targeted follow-up system reduces unnecessary measurements while preserving accurate records, allowing astronauts to focus on health indicators that require attention. Ultimately, the project aims to promote greater astronaut independence in recognising potential health risks and taking appropriate action during long-duration missions, when immediate medical assistance from Earth may not be available.

Orbit Health is an educational prototype rather than a certified medical device. Its demonstration ranges are not clinically validated, and the application does not diagnose medical conditions, contact medical personnel, or replace established mission medical procedures.
